summary: Tenant multiplex leak causing sustained 5xx wave and runtime exit-loop under mixed streaming+embedding load
description:
Issue summary:
Customer SynthScale reported sharp increase in 5xx errors starting 2026-03-12 09:14 UTC concurrent with a large mixed workload (long-lived streaming chats + large embedding batch uploads).

Impact:
- ~18% error rate on tenant requests for 30+ minutes with many clients experiencing failed streaming sessions and failing embedding uploads.
- Several runtime pods entered an exit-loop (watchdog-triggered restarts) causing repeated upstream 502/503s at the API gateway.
- Customer reports degraded UX: streaming sessions drop after initial tokens and embeddings fail with 5xx during upload retries.

Occurrence pattern / hypothesis:
- Appears tied to tenant connection multiplexing: a leak of ephemeral session handles in the ingress proxy results in an inflated in-flight connection count for the tenant.
- Influx of multiplexed streaming + embedding batches triggers aggressive prefetch and kvcache writes; kvcache lock contention then causes serving runtime threads to block, eventually tripping GPU watchdog restarts.

Environment:
- Dedicated tenant in prod(us-east-1) on Dedicated pool-d-5
- API gateway version: v2.33.1
- Serving runtime image: redwood/serving-runtime:2026-02-27-abcdef

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Large client opens ~120 persistent streaming connections with keepalive.
2) Same client launches concurrent embedding bulk upload (multi-part, 1000 vectors) while streams active.
3) Within 90s, keepalive counters at ingress show sustained half-open socket count growth and multiplex handles per worker exceed expected thresholds.
4) Serving runtime CPU thread saturation and kv-cache write latencies spike.
5) GPU watchdog resets occur, runtime pods restart, API gateway surfaces 502/503/504 to clients.

Relevant log excerpts:
- ingress-proxy: "WARN conn_pool: leaked_handle tenant_id=sst-88f, handle_id=0x7f9a5a2c"
- api-gateway: "ERROR upstream 502 fn=proxy_request tenant=sst-88f backend=runtime-42 status=BAD_UPSTREAM"
- runtime kernel: "E NVML: GPU watchdog reset triggered by driver NVML_ERROR_UNKNOWN"
- runtime app: "ERROR worker: prefetch_task stuck waiting on kvcache: shard=12 lock_wait=1234ms"

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Support throttled tenant concurrency at the gateway for synthscale via per-tenant limit (rate limit reduced to 50 concurrent streams) at 2026-03-12 10:03 UTC — observed error rate drop to 2.6% within 6 minutes.
- Evicted and cycled affected runtime pool nodes to break stuck prefetch/kvcache locks.

Requested next actions / ask from Engineering:
- SRE/Eng to investigate potential leak in ingress multiplex handle accounting and add guard rails to prevent handle growth beyond threshold.
- Add runtime circuit-breaker to abort heavy prefetch/kvcache operations when lock wait > 500ms to avoid blocking GPU watchdog-critical threads.
- Collect full pprof / thread dumps from a sample runtime pod immediately when lock_wait exceeds 200ms.

Customer notes:
- Customer provided request IDs and client timestamps (attached). They are on a dedicated contract and need an RCA and remediation timeline for production hardening.

Attachments:
- synthscale_request_ids_2026-03-12.csv (attached to ticket)
comments: 2026-03-12 09:31 - Support (Aisha Patel): Initial customer report received via email. Logged request IDs and escalated to SRE. Notified on Slack #support-synthscale.

2026-03-12 09:45 - SRE (Marco Ruiz): Observed ingress handle growth on prod-us-east. Short-term mitigation: apply per-tenant concurrency cap and drain one runtime pool. Implemented at 10:03 UTC. Monitoring now.

2026-03-12 10:12 - Customer (SynthScale - Elena M.): Confirming partial recovery — streaming stability improved but some embedding uploads still get 5xx. Asked for ETA on permanent fix and whether we can whitelist brief higher burst for scheduled jobs.

2026-03-12 13:05 - Eng (Dmitri Volkov): Running heap/profile captures from a restarted runtime pod. Early signs point to kvcache shard lock hot-spot; opening PR for lock-timeout guard. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4120

2026-03-13 08:22 - SRE (Marco Ruiz): Confirmed PR merged to canary with a 500ms kvcache lock abort. Monitoring canary for 24h then roll to prod. Noted a required follow-up: ingress multiplex metrics need an alert (MAX_HANDLES > 80).
investigation_notes:
- Trace of tenant sst-88f shows handle leakage pattern: delta(handles) outpaces delta(close) under mixed workload.
- kvcache instrumentation indicates heavy write amplification during concurrent embedding multi-part uploads.
- GPU watchdog triggers correlated with long-stalled threads in runtime (threads waiting on kvcache shard locks).
- No immediate OOM in pod; restarts are watchdog-triggered watchdog resets reported by NVML.
- Reproducer: synthetic load runner opened 130 streams + concurrent 10k vector embedding upload reproduces the issue locally on dedicated-sim cluster.
- Hypothesis: ingress proxy improperly reuses/retains multiplex handles for streaming connections when concurrent large multipart uploads pause socket flush, leading to logical connection count > physical limit and kvcache thrash.

Open questions:
- Is there a race in ingress-proxy's handle lifecycle during multi-part uploads with long-lived streams?
- Should the gateway enforce hard per-tenant multiplex limits earlier (reject vs queue)?

Telemetry/dashboard links:
- Metrics: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ingress/tenant-handles?orgId=1&var-tenant=sst-88f
- Logs: https://logs.redwood.ai/synthscale/requests?from=2026-03-12T09:00&to=2026-03-12T11:00
- Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C01234567/p1678600000000
resolution: Mitigation in-place: per-tenant concurrency cap and runtime pool recycle reduced error rate. Engineering to roll kvcache lock-timeout guard to prod. Permanent fix pending canary validation and ingress-proxy leak patch.
next_steps: 1) Monitor canary for 24h after kvcache-guard rollout. 2) Add ingress multiplex handle alert (MAX_HANDLES > 80) and automated soft-rejecting policy. 3) Schedule RCA write-up and follow-up with customer by 2026-03-17.
resolution_notes: Temporary throttle applied and nodes cycled. PR merged to canary for kvcache lock abort. Pending ingress-proxy fix and automated alerting. Customer updated 2026-03-13.
public_communication: We informed the customer of a temporary mitigation and that a code change to limit kvcache lock wait is in canary. Committing to an RCA and roadmap for ingress hard-limits by 2026-03-17.
